key_insight: Memory-bounded tensor operators enable large-scale topology optimization in JAX without materializing memory-intensive finite-element intermediates.
engineering_relevance: The approach makes high-level CPU/GPU programming practical for large 3D structural optimization while reducing reliance on specialized low-level implementations.
method: Evaluate matrix-free fine-grid stiffness actions in overlapping spatial slices.
Factorize coarse-grid operators using fine-grid stiffness interpolation coefficients and precomputed local operators, preserving the exact Galerkin hierarchy.
Implement the operators in topax, a modular JAX library for 2D and 3D density-based topology optimization.
evidence_signal: On one NVIDIA GH200, topax completes 50 design iterations with over 809 million displacement degrees of freedom in approximately 24.5 minutes; across the common GPU benchmark, it is up to 13.6× faster than the fastest competitor and uses less than half the device memory for the largest problem.
watch_item: Reported speed and memory gains are benchmark-specific; performance on other hardware and problem settings requires validation.
paper_title: Sliced Tensor Operators for Large-Scale Topology Optimization
